Warren recorded seven of his 11 outs via the strikeout, racking up 13 whiffs on 28 swings and flashing the kind of swing-and-miss stuff that could be valuable in the Yankees bullpen.
“He can be big for us moving forward in the postseason, and in different roles,” manager Aaron Boone said.
The Yankees know they have workhorses Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn to form the bridge to David Bednar in the ninth inning, but they could certainly use more help. Warren has a chance to offer it, especially as his velocity and stuff has ticked up over the past month.
“I feel like as a starter, you’re supposed to get both sides of the plate out, so I think that would be pretty big for us,” said Warren, who finished the season with a 3.92 ERA. “You see Blackburn do it, you see Headrick do it, so whenever my name’s called, I’ll be ready to go.”
The club kept Warren to 54 pitches Friday in his third relief appearance of the season, ensuring he will be available on Tuesday for Game 1 against the Red Sox while also offering some length if needed.
“I felt good — a little less blackout this time,” Warren joked, referring to his bullpen cameo earlier this month against the Padres.
On a day when the wind from the incoming nor’easter wreaked some havoc, the Yankees (93-68) dropped the first game of the doubleheader 10-2 before taking the nightcap. Whether they actually play Game 162 on Sunday remains to be seen, with the forecast iffy, but their bats came alive in the second half of the twin bill, including a two-run double from Anthony Volpe and two hits apiece from Ben Rice and Ryan McMahon.
Former Met Pete Alonso crushed a pair of home runs for the Orioles (79-82) in Game 1 — including a 471-foot shot that cut through the wind blowing in — to move into sole possession of the American League lead with 43 on the year.
The Yankees also had some questionable outfield defense in both ends of the doubleheader, windy or not. In Game 1, Spencer Jones could not track down a fly ball to center field, as it hit off his glove and turned into an inside-the-park home run for Jeremiah Jackson. In Game 2, right fielder Heliot Ramos simply dropped a fly ball to right field.

With the New York Yankees locked into an American League Wild Card berth, anticipation is building around who will make the final postseason roster—especially after former AL Rookie of the Year Luis Gil was optioned to the Florida Complex League ahead of October.
Gil was optioned alongside fellow right-hander Bradley Hanner, leaving one final roster spot up for grabs, as the Yankees announced on Thursday. While Gil had an opportunity to pitch his way onto the October roster, a rocky, walk-heavy outing against the Tampa Bay Rays sealed his fate.
In addition to bullpen decisions, the Yankees are closely monitoring their key injured stars as October approaches. On that front, manager Aaron Boone addressed the media to clear the air regarding conflicting reports about Aaron Judge’s status.
Boone also remains hopeful that slugger Giancarlo Stanton can return in time for the postseason, as the organization continues evaluating his physical readiness through live drills and simulated games.
Luis Gil #81 of the New York Yankees throws a pitch.
Yankees’ potential postseason roster
While the front office awaits definitive health updates on Judge, Stanton, and outfielder Trent Grisham, the baseline roster is coming into focus for their Wild Card showdown against the archrival Boston Red Sox, who are facing injury concerns of their own regarding catcher Willson Contreras.
Here is how the Yankees’ postseason roster is projecting:
- Starting Rotation: Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodón, Cam Schlittler, Will Warren
- Relief Pitchers: David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Michael Fulmer, Brent Headrick, Tim Hill, John Schreiber, Ryan Yarbrough
- Catchers: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez
- Infielders: Jazz Chisholm Jr., Paul Goldschmidt, Ryan McMahon, Anthony Volpe, José Caballero, Luis García Jr., Amed Rosario, George Lombard Jr., Ben Rice (1B/DH)
- Outfielders: Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, Spencer Jones
As New York prepares for October baseball, fans are eager to watch the latest chapter in the game’s greatest rivalry unfold, with a spot in the ALDS against the division-champion Tampa Bay Rays hanging in the balance.
Key takeaways
- Luis Gil was optioned to the Florida Complex League ahead of October.
- Aaron Boone addressed conflicting media reports regarding Aaron Judge’s status.
- New York projects Gerrit Cole to lead its postseason starting rotation.

item.content:encoded:
Clarke Schmidt is back on the shelf with another injury.
The Yankees announced Thursday afternoon that the righty is being placed on the 15-day IL with right bicep neuritis, retroactive to Sept. 21. Schmidt had hoped to throw on Thursday, but that was nixed as his arm discomfort lingered. He was warming up in the bullpen in Sunday's series finale against the Diamondbacks, but cut it short due to what he described as "bicep cramps." Schmidt told reporters after the game that it was a precautionary measure.
Schmidt played catch on Tuesday and Wednesday as he tried to shake the bicep troubles, but it did not improve, meaning he will not be an option for the Wild Card Series against the Red Sox, which begins on Tuesday night.
Schmidt had recently returned from Tommy John surgery, and will finish the regular season having made just one appearance in relief, tossing 0.2 innings.
The injury to Schmidt is the latest blow for a Yankee team counting on injured pitchers to return and give their beleaguered bullpen a boost for the postseason. Ryan Weathers, who was having a splendid season before landing on the IL, was seen as a good bet to return in time to make an impact in relief come October, but he is no longer expected to be ready before the end of the regular season, making it hard to imagine he will be on the Wild Card Series roster. Brent Headrick has looked more human of late as his heavy workload continues, and Fernando Cruz is still trying to make his way back from a partially torn UCL.
A potential bullpen option is off the table for the Wild Card Series.

The New York Yankees have three main arms in their bullpen who they can rely on during the postseason. This trio of relievers consists of closer David Bednar, Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn, the Yankees' best relief assets all season.
But who can they count on in the trust tree behind these three relief pitchers? Let's try to project which bullpen arms the Yankees can lean on in the playoffs from most to least trustworthy.
Yankees' most trustworthy relievers as playoffs approach
Yankees manager Aaron Boone has Bednar, Headrick and Blackburn, who he can go to in the late innings if the team has the lead or is in a tie game. But the Yankees are going to need more than that if they're going to make a deep run.
This is where Will Warren will likely come in as someone that can give the Yankees some key innings in long relief in the playoffs. Warren has not allowed a run in three innings as a reliever this season, and has pitched well as of late overall (2.45 ERA in September).
Hear me out on this next one: If Tim Hill makes the postseason roster, he will step up for the Yankees. Hill has allowed just one earned run across 11.1 playoff innings for the Yankees in the last two years. Since May 31, Hill has seen his ERA balloon from 2.53 to 4.71. But he is postseason tested, which means Boone and the Yankees should be able to count on him.
Last but not least, the sixth most trustworthy bullpen option could be newcomer John Schreiber. The right-hander has a 2.00 ERA over nine innings since joining the Yankees at the beginning of the month. Like Hill, Schreiber has postseason success, posting five scoreless relief appearances against the Yankees, ironically, in the 2024 postseason while pitching for the Kansas City Royals.
Who the Yankees shouldn't trust in ther playoff bullpen
Now we get to the part, where the names on this list probably should be pitching in lower leverage spots in the postseason. Fernando Cruz would've been included here, but his return is in doubt due to a partially torn UCL in his right elbow. Beyond Cruz, there is a pair of starters who are coming back from injury that likely can't be trusted at this point.
No. 1 is Clarke Schmidt, who just experienced biceps soreness when trying to warm up in the bullpen on Sunday. Schmidt came back from 2025 Tommy John surgery on September 16, but has been limited to one appearance, where he recorded two outs. It's hard to see how he could be high up on the trust tree in the postseason if the Yankees keep him on the playoff roster.
The second starter is Ryan Weathers, who had a breakout season for the Yankees this year. The expectation was that Weathers could be a solid relief option in the playoffs, but he is now unlikely to return in the regular season due to his left forearm flexor strain. It's difficult to envision Weathers coming back healthy at this point and being a trusted reliever in the biggest games of the year.
Should the Yankees choose to go: Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole, Carlos Rodón, Bednar, Headrick, Blackburn, Warren, Hill, Schreiber, Weathers, Schmidt, that would mean there's one more spot available for a pitcher on a 13-man staff. This last slot would come down to: Luis Gil, Michael Fulmer or Ryan Yarbrough.
While Gil has the most upside of the three, he can be erratic with his command at times. He also has a 6.75 ERA for his career in the postseason. Fulmer has a 4.50 ERA since joining the Yankees last month and Yarbrough is better suited to give length when the team is trailing. Whoever the Yankees decide to give the last spot to will be a low leverage option and at the bottom of the trust tree.

Despite their best efforts, the New York Yankees are all but guaranteed to face the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card Series. Like any time the two heated rivals face off against each other, the three-game set will almost certainly push both teams to do whatever it takes to gain an advantage. For the Yankees, that could mean adding a few surprising players on the roster that you might not expect.
With the Yankees nearly a lock to play the Red Sox, manager Aaron Boone has already been eyeing his likely starting rotation in preparation for the postseason. The Yankees will likely roll with a combination of Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, and Gerrit Cole. That rotation would likely lead to some creativity when it comes to how the rest of the roster is constructed.
That creativity could potentially be used exclusively within the team’s bullpen. Would that mean that Carlos Rodón is left off the roster for the short series in favor of a pitcher more capable of coming out of the pen? With plenty of tough innings between the Yankees and Red Sox coming up, there could be some surprise arms out of the bullpen to bridge the gap between the starters and closer David Bednar.
3 surprise pitchers who could give the Yankees valuable innings in the postseason
Over the last few weeks of the season, relievers Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn have seemed to be feeling the effects of a long season where they have each thrown more than 77 innings. With that wear and tear weighing on their shoulders, they have both looked a little more human as of late. That doesn’t mean that they won’t step up when it matters the most in the postseason, but they may need some help.
The Yankees will need to collect at least 54 outs against the Red Sox in order to move on to the Divisional round. When it comes to the postseason, it doesn’t matter how you get those outs. In fact, it doesn’t even matter who gets those outs for you. For the Yankees, they could be giving the ball to a few pitchers that may turn some heads.
Ryan Weathers
While his battle with a nagging elbow flexor strain could complicate things, Ryan Weathers has the potential to become a game-changing pitcher for the Yankees in the Wild Card round. Out since August, Weathers may not come back in time to finish out the regular season. With the Yankees’ first postseason game scheduled for September 29, that doesn’t leave a lot of time for Weathers to make it back for a matchup against the Red Sox, either.
But if he can bounce back and throw an inning or two, Weathers may become one of the team’s most valuable weapons out of the pen. With a 9.4 K/9 rate this season, the southpaw is more than capable of picking up a much-needed punchout to quell a potential rally. Perhaps more importantly, he’s induced nine ground ball double plays in high-leverage situations this season.
If healthy enough to pitch, Weathers could be an effective option for Boone. That would go a long way toward saving relievers like Headrick and Blackburn for the later innings if needed.
Yerry de los Santos
With only three games to worry about in the Wild Card round, Boone could easily look to add as many versatile relievers as possible. Yerry de los Santos may not be the first name you'd think of when considering a lockdown postseason bullpen, but he could become a valuable arm against the Red Sox.
His propensity to fill the base paths with runners isn't exactly the best formula for postseason success. With a career WHIP of 1.334, it would be very unlikely that Boone would turn to de los Santos in a close game. But in the event of a blowout in either of the first two games, de los Santos would become the best option to eat innings and save the high-leverage arms for the next day. That could be invaluable in the long run.
With a high ground ball rate and an ability to miss barrels, de los Santos has been good at limiting the damage during his time with the Yankees. That could continue against the Red Sox. Just don't expect to see him jogging in from the bullpen in a tight one (even though he was briefly RP4, almost by default, in mid-August).
Elmer Rodriguez
After looking like a whole new pitcher following his most recent call up in August, Elmer Rodriguez offered fans a glimpse into his future as a postseason starter. Maybe just not this year, though. But that doesn't mean he won't be a big factor in the Wild Card round.
With an impressive combination of a power sinker and a four-seamer, Rodriguez is capable of getting ahead of hitters and establishing his fastball. This could allow him to set up his strong offering of breaking balls. On the season, batters are slugging just .182 off the sweeper and an embarrassingly low .091 off of his curveball.
As a short relief option, Rodriguez could see an uptick in velocity that would better play off of his breaking balls. With wipeout stuff, Rodriguez could be yet another surprise weapon for Boone to unleash out of the bullpen.

Updated Yankees projected Wild Card Series roster without Aaron Judge
NEW YORK - Here was the scenario these Yankees hoped to avoid, but couldn't - a triumphant Tampa Bay Rays team, celebrating their AL East title on Bronx turf.
"They've put together a fantastic regular season to earn that,'' said manager Aaron Boone, after the Rays' 6-1 victory in Tuesday's nightcap of a split doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
"Hopefully, we get another crack at them.''
That would be in a best-of-five AL Division Series, but only if the Yankees advance from a best-of-three Wild Card series, which they'll host - likely against the rival Red Sox.
With that Wild Card opponent in mind, here is our updated version of a Yankees 26-man playoff roster (12 pitchers, 14 position players), for a series that would begin on Tuesday, Sept. 29.
Rosters can be altered before each postseason round. Injured players can be replaced in-series (pitcher for pitcher, position player for position player) but the injured player is ineligible for the next playoff series.
Projected Yankees pitchers (12)
Starters (3): RHPs Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole; LHP Max Fried.
Relievers (9): RHPs David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Will Warren, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber; LHPs Ryan Weathers, Tim Hill, Brent Headrick, Carlos Rodon.
On the bubble: RHPs Clarke Schmidt.
Also available: RHPs Luis Gil, Elmer Rodriguez, Yerry de los Santos, Bradley Hanner, Carlos Lagrange; LHP Ryan Yarbrough.
Currently injured: RHPs Fernando Cruz, Angel Chivilli, Kervin Castro.
Analysis: Would the Yanks start anyone but Schlittler in Game 1?
Well, nothing's been firmly stated about the first round rotation, though Schlittler - the odds-on choice for the AL Cy Young Award - would be on normal rest for the opener.
Cole (Wednesday) and Schlittler (Thursday) will make their final regular season starts during this Rays series, though Boone mentioned limiting both starters in these tune-ups for postseason.
In the bullpen, Schmidt's recent bout of biceps cramping wasn't fully resolved as of Tuesday; he was due to be re-examined after a throwing session.
It's possible that even a slight setback takes Schmidt out of consideration for an important playoff spot, moving Michael Fulmer off the bubble and on the roster.
Rodon's eight shutout innings in Tuesday's doubleheader opener was his best effort, during an impressive stretch drive.
He'd be certain to start Game 1 or 2 of a Division Series vs. the Rays, but the Yanks might need his services - in some capacity - to advance vs. Boston, so he's now included here.
Projected Yankees infielders, utility/DH (9)
Infielders (7): Luis Garcia Jr., 1B; Paul Goldschmidt, 1B; Ben Rice, 1B-DH; Jazz Chisholm Jr., 2B; George Lombard Jr., SS; Anthony Volpe, 2B-SS; Ryan McMahon, 3B.
Utility players: (2): Jose Caballero, IF-OF; Amed Rosario, 3B-2B.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: Max Schuemann.
Analysis: Garcia and McMahon are slumping at the wrong time, while Chisholm - who just returned off the IL (right thumb sprain) on Tuesday - has this week to find his rhythm again at the plate.
But that trio of lefty hitters might all be starting on the bench against Boston, which could employ three lefty starters against the Yanks.
That puts Caballero in play as a third base option, with the veteran Goldschmidt (.997 OPS vs. lefties) at first base, the rookie Lombard at short, and Volpe recast as a second baseman.
Projected Yankees outfielders (3)
Cody Bellinger, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: Jasson Dominguez.
Currently injured: Aaron Judge, Trent Grisham.
Analysis: That's a thin outfield without Judge, whom the Yanks are not planning to have for at least the Wild Card series - per Boone - due to the captain's "moderate'' right calf strain.
It's increasingly unlikely that Grisham (strained hamstring) is available, too, by next week, and that presents a danger considering Ramos' defensive deficiencies.
For that same reason, Dominguez is on the outside. Mostly, the Yanks need the potent right-handed bats of Ramos (who has found his hitting groove) and Rosario to combat Boston's lefty pitching.
Caballero could find himself pressed into outfield duty, too.
Without Judge, "it's going to be super tough on us,'' said Ramos. "But we're going to go forward, for sure.''
Yankees' projected catchers (2)
Austin Wells, Ali Sanchez.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: J.C. Escarra.
Analysis: Wells has been a better offensive presence after a brutal first half, and Sanchez has learned the staff and he earned much praise from Rodon for his contribution to Tuesday's game one win.
Boone has kept the Cole-Wells pairing together, and you'd still anticipate Wells getting starts vs. Boston's lefty starters throughout this opening series.

item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK – La noticia sobre el regreso de Aaron Judge a la lista de lesionados aún estaba fresca, habiendo sido anunciada menos de una hora antes, y ya Cody Bellinger estaba imaginando cómo los Yankees podían tener éxito en la postemporada sin su capitán.
Desafortunadamente para Judge y su club, han tenido mucha práctica haciendo exactamente eso esta temporada. No han tenido otra opción.
"Falta Judge y duele", dijo Bellinger. "Todos sabemos que él es el mejor bateador del juego. Para nosotros aquí, nuestra mentalidad es que vamos a tener que encontrar la manera. Creo que el talento en este clubhouse habla por sí mismo. Estoy completamente seguro de que tenemos suficiente talento aquí para salir, ganar y vencer a cualquiera.
Ahora tendrán su oportunidad para demostrarlo.
El manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone, confirmó el martes que Judge está lidiando con un esguince "moderado" de la pantorrilla derecha y no se espera que esté listo para una posible Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas, que comenzaría el 29 de septiembre.
La disponibilidad de Judge para las rondas posteriores, especialmente la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana, también está en duda. Pero los Yankees necesitan llegar allí primero. Aquí hay cinco motivos por los que los Yankees, elogiados como favoritos para ganar el banderín, aún pueden llegar a la Serie Mundial incluso si Judge no regresa:
Lanzadores abridores dominantes
**
Cuando Carlos Rodón lanzó ocho entradas sin permitir carreras en la **victoria por 2-0 del martes sobre los Rays, no sólo mantuvo el champán en el clubhouse de Tampa Bay (por el momento), sino que también sirvió como un recordatorio de la mayor fortaleza de los Yankees.
Rodón podría ni siquiera abrir un partido en una posible Serie de Comodines, quedando detrás de los favoritos al premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole y Max Fried. En pocas palabras, la rotación los ha mantenido a flote.
Los abridores de los Yankees han permitido dos carreras limpias o menos en 40 de 51 aperturas desde el 28 de julio, incluyendo una carrera limpia o menos en 33 de esas aperturas, acumulando efectividad de 2.50 en ese período. En general, han permitido una carrera o menos en 65 encuentros, un récord de franquicia en una sola campaña.
"Venimos a ganar cada partido, sin importar quién esté en el terreno", dijo Rodón. "Obviamente, es difícil cuando no tienes al mejor jugador del mundo en el terreno contigo. Tengo la esperanza de que vuelva. Pero... se trata simplemente de ganar juegos para nosotros.
Hay otro trueno
Esto no es el 2022, cuando los 62 jonrones de Judge establecieron un récord de la Liga Americana para una sola temporada y sirvieron como el motor indiscutible de la ofensiva. Principalmente debido a la lesión en la costilla, Judge se limitó a un promedio de .241, 18 vuelacercas y 41 impulsadas en 66 encuentros. Ben Rice asumió gran parte de la carga este año, cumpliendo con la predicción de la primavera de Boone de 39 cuadrangulares.
Bellinger sigue siendo una fuerza impactante, mientras que el aumento de la velocidad del bate del dominicano Luis García Jr. sugiere que su producción es sostenible, a pesar de una reciente caída. Mientras tanto, el puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos ha mostrado poder después de un comienzo lento y se confiará en él en los playoffs contra lanzadores zurdos.
"Sabemos que somos capaces de ganar partidos", dijo Boone, quien señaló el récord de 36-24 del club desde el descanso del Juego de las Estrellas, la mayor parte del cual ocurrió sin Judge. "Nos hemos tenido que enfrentar a jugar sin muchas piezas clave en diferentes momentos y durante grandes tramos de esta campaña”.
**Los jóvenes pueden dar la cara
**
El cubano-estadounidense George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones llamaron la atención durante la reciente serie del club contra los Diamondbacks, cuando dieron jonrones con un total combinado de 872 pies calculados por Statcast contra Corbin Burnes – potentes batazos de 424 y 448 pies, respectivamente, que sugieren que se están sintiendo más cómodos en Grandes Ligas.
Ha habido algunos obstáculos durante sus primeros meses de actividad en las Mayores, con Lombard cometiendo errores en seis compromisos consecutivos en un período y Jones mostrando los swings en blanco que probablemente siempre sean parte de su juego. Pero el talento es real y nadie debería sorprenderse si alguno de los novatos brilla en un gran momento de octubre.
"Realmente sólo tenemos que jugar uno para el otro; apoyarnos mutuamente, pasar la batuta", dijo Bellinger. "Haces tu trabajo y controlas lo que puedes”.
Mejorando la salud
Mientras la situación de Judge no está clara, los Yankees están volviendo lentamente a estar completos.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. fue activado de la lista de lesionados entre los juego de la doble-jornada del martes, restaurando una presencia dinámica. Ha sido un año decepcionante en general, pero Chisholm estaba en racha en el momento de su lesión (de 46-18, .391). Los Yankees esperarán que retome eso.
Mientras tanto, Anthony Volpe aprovechó al máximo una oportunidad ante la ausencia de Chisholm, lo que podría haberle valido un lugar en el roster de playoffs, especialmente si los Yankees optan por contar con 11 lanzadores y 15 jugadores de posición en la primera ronda. Se cree que Trent Grisham está en la contienda para el roster.
"Con suerte, más personas podrán unirse y hacernos más formidables en el camino", dijo Boone.
Un bullpen reforzado
Los relevistas de los Yankees han estado entre los mejores de Grandes Ligas todo el año, pero ha habido señales preocupantes últimamente. Brent Headrick ocupa el segundo lugar en las Grandes Ligas con 79 presentaciones y ha mostrado una velocidad inconsistente. Mientras tanto, David Bednar y Paul Blackburn siguen en buena forma.
Debido a que los Yankees no tendrían por qué para a tener cinco abridores en octubre, la ayuda está en camino. Will Warren tiene programada una última apertura y luego pasará a un rol de relevista, dando al bullpen una opción intrigante de múltiples entradas. Clarke Schmidt y Ryan Weathers también están en consideración.
"Eso es lo bueno de la postemporada; los muchachos caen en diferentes roles y muchas veces pueden ser heroicos en papeles que no necesariamente imaginabas al inicio de la temporada", expresó Boone.

NEW YORK – The news about Aaron Judge’s return to the injured list was still fresh, having been announced less than an hour earlier, and already Cody Bellinger was envisioning how the Yankees could succeed in the postseason without their captain.
Unfortunately for Judge and his club, they’ve had plenty of practice doing exactly that this season. They’ve had no choice.
“Missing Judge, it hurts,” Bellinger said. “We all know he’s the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is, we’re going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I’m fully confident that we have enough talent in here to go out, win and beat anybody.”
Now they’ll have their chance to prove it.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Tuesday that Judge is dealing with a “moderate” strain of his right calf and is not expected to be ready for a potential American League Wild Card Series against the Red Sox, which would begin on Sept. 29.
Judge’s availability for subsequent rounds, especially the AL Division Series, is also in doubt. But the Yankees need to get there first. Here are five reasons why the Yankees, lauded as pennant favorites, still can reach the Fall Classic even if Judge doesn’t return:
Dominant starting pitching
Rodón might not even draw a start in a potential Wild Card Series, standing in line behind AL Cy Young Award frontrunner Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole and Max Fried. Simply put, the rotation has kept them afloat.
Yankees starters have permitted two earned runs or fewer in 40 of 51 starts since July 28, including one earned run or fewer in 33 of those starts, compiling a 2.50 ERA over that span. Overall, they’ve allowed one run or fewer in 65 games, a single-season franchise record.
“We come to win every game, regardless of who is on the field,” Rodón said. “Obviously it’s tough when you don’t have the best player in the world on the field with you. I’m hopeful that he’ll be back. But … it’s just about winning games for us.”
There’s other thump
This isn’t 2022, when Judge’s 62 home runs set a single-season AL record and served as the unquestioned engine of the offense. Mostly because of the rib injury, Judge was limited to a .241 average, 18 homers and 41 RBIs across 66 games. Ben Rice shouldered much of the load, fulfilling Boone’s spring prediction of 39 homers.
Bellinger remains an impactful force, while Luis García Jr.’s increased bat speed suggests his production is sustainable despite a recent slump. Meanwhile, Heliot Ramos has shown power after a sluggish start and will be leaned upon in the playoffs against left-handed pitching.
“We know we’re capable of winning games,” said Boone, who noted the club’s 36-24 record since the All-Star break, most of which occurred without Judge. “We’ve had to play without a lot of key pieces at different points and for large chunks of this season.”
The kids are all right
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones opened eyes during the club’s recent series against the Diamondbacks, when they crushed a Statcast-calculated combined 872 feet of home runs against Corbin Burnes – big-boy blasts of 424 and 448 feet, respectively, that suggested they’re growing more comfortable in The Show.
There have been growing pains across their first months of big league activity, with Lombard committing errors in six consecutive games over one span and Jones showing the swing-and-miss that will probably always be part of his game. But the talent is real, and no one should be surprised if either rookie delivers in a big October moment.
“We really just have to play for each other; lean on each other, pass the baton,” Bellinger said. “You do your job and control what you can.”
Improving health
While Judge’s outlook is cloudy, the Yankees are slowly becoming more whole.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. was activated from the injured list between games of Tuesday’s doubleheader, restoring a dynamic presence. It has been a disappointing year overall, but Chisholm was hot at the time of his injury (18-for-46, .391). The Yanks will look for him to pick up where he left off.
Meanwhile, Anthony Volpe made the most of an opportunity in Chisholm’s absence, which could have earned him a spot on a playoff roster – especially if they go with 11 pitchers and 15 position players in the first round. Trent Grisham is thought to be in play for the playoff roster.
“Hopefully more people are able to join and make us more formidable along the way,” Boone said.
A bolstered bullpen
The Yankees’ relievers have been among the league’s best all year, but there have been concerning signs of late. Brent Headrick ranks second in the Majors with 79 appearances and has seen inconsistent velocity, for example, suggesting he could benefit from a breather once the AL East is decided. David Bednar and Paul Blackburn, meanwhile, remain sharp.
Because the Yankees would have no reason to roster five starting pitchers in October, help is on the way. Will Warren is scheduled to make one more start and then transition to a relief role, giving the ’pen an intriguing multi-inning option. Clarke Schmidt and Ryan Weathers are also in the mix.
“That’s the beauty of the postseason; guys fall into different roles and a lot of times can become heroic in roles you didn’t necessarily count on at the start of the season,” Boone said.

item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays will get two chances to clinch their first American League East title since 2021 when they visit the New York Yankees for a day/night doubleheader on Tuesday.
With a magic number of two over the Yankees, the Rays can seal their fate in the afternoon opener.
Tampa Bay (95-60) has won six of the nine games against New York and owns a six-game lead on the Yankees. New York (89-66) has a magic number of two for clinching the AL's top wild-card spot over the Boston Red Sox.
The Rays, who are seeking their fifth division title, have led the AL East every day since June 27.
Following a 2-7 run last month, Tampa Bay is 19-7 since Aug. 23 and just went 8-1 on a homestand against the Houston Astros, Athletics and Red Sox. It featured three walk-off wins and ended with Sunday's 5-1 win over Boston which saw Chandler Simpson and Jonny DeLuca drive in two runs apiece.
"We knew what we had to do," Tampa Bay pitcher Griffin Jax said. "We wanted to put ourselves in a good place going into New York, make it a little bit easier."
The Yankees play host to the Rays for the first time since Aaron Judge's game-ending two-run homer for a 2-0 victory May 24. Judge returned Sept. 8 after missing 84 games with a fractured rib, played seven games and returned to the injured list with a strained calf.
The Yankees are 48-41 in games Judge has not played and enter the upcoming series after losing two of three at Arizona, including an 8-4 loss Sunday. Rookies George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones hit two of New York's three home runs in the third inning, but Brent Headrick gave up a grand slam to Arizona's Nolan Arenado in the fifth.
"We're going to show up and try to win the games on Tuesday, and then we'll keep going from there," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "We've been through a lot as a team this year already, and we've answered the bell at the turns. We're looking forward to hopefully playing a good week of baseball and building some momentum going into the postseason."
Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94 ERA) will start the opener for Tampa Bay followed by Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) in the second game. Martinez is 3-0 with a 2.43 ERA in his past five starts and 2-2 with a 4.30 ERA in 12 career appearances against the Yankees.
Since allowing six runs in 2 1/3 innings at home against the Yankees on July 9, Rasmussen is 8-0 with a 1.91 ERA in his past 11 starts. He is 4-2 with a 1.87 ERA in 10 career outings against the Yankees.
New York will start Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95) in the opener followed by Max Fried (5-4, 2.63).
Rodon is 2-1 with a 2.40 ERA in six starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 18 and is 3-3 with a 3.88 ERA in 10 career starts against the Rays
Fried is 1-0 with a 1.83 ERA in four starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 29 and allowed one run in seven innings last Tuesday at Minnesota. He is 5-0 with a 1.26 ERA in six career starts against Tampa Bay.

item.content:encoded:
It's funny to think that at one point it felt like sacrilege to even consider trading Luis Gil for anyone. Here was the prospective American League Rookie of the Year who held it down in the rotation while Gerrit Cole was sidelined for much of 2024, and the Houston Astros wanted him as the centerpiece of a trade for Kyle Tucker. The New York Yankees scoffed at the idea and opted to keep Gil.
In hindsight, they should have landed Tucker and sent Gil to Houston. Gil immediately broke down, and his velocity has never been what it was during his first full season, when he earned rookie honors. It's a trade they likely would have won even if Tucker ended up still going to the Los Angeles Dodgers.
That one successful year feels like a lifetime ago, but now the Yankees have a chance to salvage some of his value. With injuries to Ryan Weathers, a Clarke Schmidt scare this past week, and Brent Headrick's velocity alarmingly down over the weekend, the bullpen is looking shaky heading into the postseason. With just a week left in the regular season, they should use this opportunity to see what they have in Gil.
In the best-case scenario, Gil would be relegated to lower-leverage situations. That is how they have used him, too. Gil has seen just five appearances over the last month, but things feel a little more dire, and Boone used him twice in their most recent series against the Arizona Diamondbacks. It could be a signal that they're giving Gil one last chance to prove himself. There might not be another choice, either.
The best use of Gil moving forward
Call it a bit of a Hail Mary, but it wouldn't hurt the Yankees at this point if they used Gil in medium- to high-leverage situations against the Tampa Bay Rays and Baltimore Orioles. If he can hack it, at least they know what they have. The same goes if he fails there. At least they know not to use him in that role in the postseason.
Better to find out now, when the games don't matter and the postseason is already set. Chances are the Rays aren't losing the next seven games and blowing the division, either.
One thing about Gil is that his velocity looks like it's up. He averaged 95.4 MPH on his fastball this season. Since being called up on August 31st, Gil has averaged 96.1 MPH. His slider velocity is up as well. He's averaging 87.1 MPH on it since the call-up. He is sitting at 85.8 MPH this season.
Gil's strikeout numbers are also slightly up in this small sample size. Since his call-up, he has pitched six innings and struck out eight with just three walks. He has allowed one earned run, but that was back in his first start.
Another thing about Gil is that the Yankees are waiting for his arm to return to what it used to be. He may never be what he once was, and with a stacked rotation, his only role as a Yankee is likely in the bullpen. That said, this final week could be one of Gil's most important.
It's an opportunity to show that he still has some value to the team, and if he's able to get outs, blowing heaters by batters this week and into the postseason, they don't have to feel all that bad about watching Tucker go elsewhere in 2025 — not that it would have mattered in the long run anyway.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

Yankees' playoff picture, Aaron Judge update and potential rotation
This wasn’t how the Yankees wanted to move into the regular season’s final week, with a four-game set against Tampa Bay.
Beginning with Tuesday’s day-night doubleheader, they’ll need to sweep the AL East leaders just to prevent the Rays from spilling champagne inside Yankee Stadium’s visiting clubhouse.
And there’s uncertainty surrounding Yankees captain Aaron Judge’s availability next week – the start of postseason − due to a right calf strain.
“We’ve been through a lot as a team this year already and we’ve answered the bell at mostly all the turns,’’ Yanks manager Aaron Boone told reporters, including the YES Network, after Sunday’s 8-4 loss at Arizona.
“(We’re) looking forward to hopefully playing a good week of baseball and building some momentum going into the postseason.’’
Here’s a look at the Yankees’ week ahead:
Yankees vs Rays with AL East race nearing its end
In winning 12 of their last 15 games, the Rays (95-60) have opened a six-game divisional lead on the Yanks (89-66).
On the verge of its first AL East title since 2021, Tampa Bay could clinch it with one win on a long Tuesday in the Bronx.
Tuesday’s opener has Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94) scheduled to oppose lefty Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95), with righty Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) vs. lefty Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) in the nightcap.
The Yanks are scheduled to start Gerrit Cole on Wednesday and Cam Schlittler on Thursday.
In the wider picture, Boone acknowledged the need to prep for next week, which includes giving important bullpen arms like Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn some added rest.
“You’ve got to make sure guys are in a good spot going in (to postseason),’’ Boone told reporters, speaking generally on Sunday.
“But we’re going to show up and try to win the games on Tuesday.’’
Aaron Judge injury update
Judge’s availability for the first playoff round remains a mystery.
This past weekend, Judge told reporters: “I’d like to be back by the postseason. That’s definitely the plan.’’
Judge said he’s played through minor calf strains before, but this current injury to the soleus muscle is a more problematic spot.
So, this will be a key week of treatment and testing to see if Judge could be available in any capacity for a first-round playoff series.
Yankees injury news as Jazz Chisholm Jr. might return
Sidelined since Sept. 9, lefty-hitting second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (right thumb sprain) could be activated from the injured list to start the Tampa Bay series.
Though he’s unlikely to be activated this week, lefty reliever Ryan Weathers (flexor strain) could find himself on a playoff roster next week in a bullpen capacity.
On the IL since Sept. 5, center fielder Trent Grisham (strained right hamstring) has progressed in his running and is also a possible postseason choice.
Recovered from Tommy John surgery rehab, right-hander Clarke Schmidt developed cramping in his right biceps area while warming up Sunday.
Schmidt did not enter the game, telling reporters it was “more precautionary…especially with the playoffs coming up,’’ in what could be an important relief role.
Initial testing revealed no shoulder or elbow issues, but Schmidt planned to be examined by the team physician Monday.
Schmidt called it “frustrating,’’ but feels “in the grand scheme, we’ll be out there soon.’’
How Yankees' playoff rotation might look
With the likelihood of the Yanks hosting a best-of-three Wild Card series beginning Tuesday, they'd have Cam Schlittler ready on regular rest vs. Boston in Game 1.
But that might not be how the Yankees set things up.
Gerrit Cole would be on one extra day of rest if he's the Game 1 choice, or the Yanks could give the ball to Max Fried with nearly a full week of rest. It's been one month since Fried's return from a second elbow bone bruise this season.
Carlos Rodon could be on a Wild Card roster in an emergency or long relief capacity, or he might be saved to start Game 1 or 2 of a best-of-five Division Series.
CC Sabathia to be honored at Yankee Stadium
Prior to Saturday night's game against the Orioles, CC Sabathia's No. 52 will be retired in a ceremony at Yankee Stadium.
He'll be the 24th Yankees player or manager so honored and the first since Paul O'Neill, who had his No. 21 retired in August 2022.

item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK -- Ha parecido inevitable que la lucha por el Este de la Liga Americana se decidiera esta semana en el Bronx.
Los Rays han encabezado la división más competitiva de Grandes Ligas durante gran parte de la temporada y no han cedido el primer lugar de la tabla desde que recuperaron la cima el 27 de junio.
Pero los Yankees siempre han estado ahí, amenazando y luego retrocediendo. Pero nunca han estado lo suficientemente lejos como para restarle importancia a lo que podría suceder esta semana.
Pues bien, llegó el momento.
Los Yankees recibirán a los Rays para una serie de cuatro juegos en el Yankee Stadium, comenzando con una doble-cartelera el martes. Gracias a la magnífica estadía de los Rays en casa y a la serie perdida por los Yankees en Phoenix frente a los Diamondbacks, la pregunta ahora es cuánto tiempo más seguirá viva esta lucha.
Los Rays llegaron a Nueva York con 6.0 juegos de ventaja en la división y apenas siete encuentros por disputarse. Una victoria de Tampa Bay eliminará a los Yankees de la lucha por la División Este y los dejará asegurados en un puesto del Comodín de la Liga Americana. Entonces, para que los Yankees tengan alguna posibilidad, deberán completar una barrida de cuatro partidos en tres días.
¿Lo que está en juego? Como dijo una vez Gerrit Cole: “Es mucho”. Entremos en materia.
¿Qué está en juego?
Rays: Ganar apenas un juego les garantizará a los Rays su primer campeonato del Este de la Liga Americana desde el 2021, otorgándoles un pase directo a la Serie Divisional y la ventaja de localía tanto en esa ronda como, si avanzan, en la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana. También necesitan una sola victoria para asegurar la serie particular contra los Yankees.
Yankees: El piloto Aaron Boone reconoce que será una “tarea muy difícil” evitar que los Rays celebren con champaña en el Bronx, pero eso es exactamente lo que pretenden hacer. Empezaron la temporada buscando cambiar la narrativa, después de quedarse cortos ante los Azulejos el año pasado. En cambio, están a punto de tener que conformarse nuevamente con un premio de consolación y verse obligados a ganar una serie al mejor de tres juegos.
¿Cómo están alineadas las rotaciones?
Rays: Enviarán a sus mejores dos abridores al montículo para la doble-cartelera del martes. Primero será el derecho veterano Nick Martínez, líder del clubhouse y su fuente más confiable de innings. Tampa Bay tiene marca de 22-7 esta temporada en los juegos iniciados por el cubano-estadounidense. Después, le tocará a Drew Rasmussen, uno de los mejores abridores de la Liga Americana. Los Rays no han perdido una apertura de Rasmussen desde el 9 de julio, con marca perfecta de 11-0 en sus presentaciones desde entonces. Martínez lanzará con un día adicional de descanso, mientras que Rasmussen trabajará con cuatro días de descanso apenas por séptima vez esta campaña. El zurdo Ian Seymour y el derecho dominicano Freddy Peralta estarían alineados para abrir el miércoles y el jueves, respectivamente.
Yankees: Carlos Rodón y Max Fried abrirán los juegos de la doble-cartelera, en ese orden. Ambos han lidiado con lesiones esta temporada, pero están recuperando su mejor nivel en el momento indicado. En tres aperturas de septiembre, Rodón tiene marca de 2-0 con efectividad de 2.08, dejando atrás un episodio de inflamación en el codo izquierdo. Después de ingresar dos veces a la lista de lesionados por una contusión ósea en el codo de lanzar, Fried tiene récord de 1-0 y promedio de carreras limpias de 1.69 en tres aperturas este mes. Cole y Cam Schlittler, favorito para ganar el Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, seguirán en el tercer y cuarto partidos de la serie, respectivamente.
¿Qué ha estado funcionando bien últimamente para cada equipo?
Rays: ¿Todo? Los Rays acaban de registrar récord de 8-1 durante su última estadía en casa de la campaña regular y han ganado cuatro series consecutivas contra los Bravos, Astros, Atléticos y Medias Rojas. Desde que fueron barridos en una serie de cuatro partidos en el Fenway Park tras la pausa del Juego de Estrellas, tienen marca de 39-18, la mejor de la Gran Carpa desde el 20 de julio. Su pitcheo abridor se ha visto particularmente sólido, con efectividad de 2.81 este mes, sólo detrás de la de los Yankees. Como de costumbre, han encontrado distintas maneras de anotar carreras, incluyendo ataques tempraneros como el del domingo y un par de jonrones para dejar en el terreno al rival por parte del candidato al JMV de la Liga Americana, el dominicano Junior Caminero.
Yankees: De repente, estos Yankees se encuentran apoyándose en la fortaleza de su pitcheo, confiando en que la ofensiva terminará respondiendo. Ben Rice conectó su 39no cuadrangular, la mayor cantidad del equipo, cumpliendo una predicción que Boone hizo durante los Entrenamientos de Primavera. Rice dijo que Boone estaba bromeando con él, quedándose con “uno o dos” por debajo de la cifra que él prefería, así que habrá que estar atentos a Rice mientras busca su 40mo vuelacercas esta semana. Austin Wells ha conectado tres bambinazos en sus últimos seis encuentros, mientras que el puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos ha volado la cerca en sus últimos dos partidos. Podría ser una pieza importante si los Yankees quieren hacerse sentir en octubre.
¿Cuáles son algunas áreas de preocupación que podrían convertirse en un problema esta semana o en la postemporada?
Rays: Muchos jugadores de los Rays han dado un paso al frente, pero el primer bate del equipo, el cubano Yandy Díaz, ha tenido un mes complicado, con línea ofensiva de .229/.286/.357 en septiembre. Él marca la pauta para la alineación, así que obviamente será importante que llegue en su mejor nivel a octubre. Y esto es realmente buscarle la quinta pata al gato, considerando que tiene marca de 3-0 con un salvamento y efectividad de 1.42 este mes, pero Bryan Baker, líder de Grandes Ligas en salvamentos, suma más bases por bolas (cuatro) que ponches (dos) en siete presentaciones durante septiembre. También necesitarán que sea dominante en la postemporada.
Yankees: Más allá del tirón en la pantorrilla derecha de Aaron Judge, un asunto que los Yankees están manejando como si fuera un secreto del estado, comienzan a surgir preocupaciones sobre el estado del bullpen. La velocidad de Brent Headrick ha disminuido y el relevista podría estar mostrando señales de fatiga después de liderar las Mayores con 79 presentaciones. Tim Hill no ha sido la máquina automática de provocar rodados de años anteriores. Michael Fulmer permitió un jonrón que decidió un juego en Arizona. Pero no hay un asunto más importante que demostrar que pueden ganar sin Judge, el motor alrededor del cual gira su ofensiva. Tienen marca de 48-41 sin él, comparada con 41-25 cuando ha estado en acción.

The New York Yankees are almost guaranteed to face the Boston Red Sox in an upcoming best-of-three Wild Card series, and can lock up homefield advantage with either a singular win in their final seven games or one Boston loss. The time is now for forecasting and getting your ducks in a row, and the Yankees have acknowledged as such; resetting Brent Headrick, for example, is more important than going all out to embarrass the Tampa Bay Rays this week.
That makes every rotation decision or perceived pattern seem magnified, especially after Boston lined up their starters for their upcoming series with the Cleveland Guardians: Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, Ranger Suárez. Is that the chips falling where they may, or is that foreshadowing? Either way, while winking and nodding, it's probably time to read similarly into the way the Yankees are handlng things.
That's why our eyebrows raised on Sunday when the Yanks revealed that Cam Schlittler and Gerrit Cole will stay on turn in the Rays series (for now), with Schlittler closing the four-game set and Cole pitching Game 3, both staying out of the doubleheader. That will leave Cole with an extra day of rest ahead of the WIld Card opener and Schlittler on normal rest. You're not saying ... ?
All the love in the world to Gerrit Cole, who got closer to securing an all-important Wild Card Series start with his strong appearance in the desert on Friday night. But given that his spot in the rotation in general has been rightly questioned, there is no world where he should start Game 1 over Schlittler. That is not even something that should be rolling around in the canals of my addled gray brain. And yet!
Yankees giving Gerrit Cole the rest he needs ahead of Wild Card Series. Will Cam Schlittler even start vs. Rays?
For now, this is all hypothetical, but ... Cole has always seemed like a candidate for a deciding Game 3, but nothing before it. Would the Yankees really dare to use him in a deciding game with three extra days of rest building up on his right arm?
And, if the Rays clinch the AL East this week and the Yankees lock down their positioning, will they use Schlittler at all in this series? Will he make a perfunctory three-inning cameo just to keep his sea legs ahead of the Sox showdown and prevent overthrowing/overcompensating? The Cy Young race between he and Dylan Cease is informally over, and Cease may not even be healthy enough to make another start. If positioning gets more solidified throughout the week, these decisions only become more fascinating.
As of now, though, before any adjustments ... it seems like there's at least a chance the Yankees are lining up Cole for Game 1 - or working him out of the picture entirely.

item.dc:creator: Matthew Schmidt
item.description: The New York Yankees opted not to add any relief pitchers at the MLB trade deadline. Why? The New York Yankees opted not to add any relief pitchers at the MLB trade deadline. Why? Because Ryan Weathers was going to end up in the bullpen, and Clarke Schmidt was due to return.
The Yankees were relying on two pitchers with extensive injury histories to solidify their bullpen in October. What could possibly go wrong?
Well, everything that could have gone wrong has gone wrong for New York.
Weathers suffered an elbow flexor strain last month and has been sidelined ever since. It now doesn't appear that the left-hander will return before the playoffs, leaving his postseason status in jeopardy.
Schmidt? He suffered a setback at the beginning of August due to forearm cramping. He then finally returned last week and pitched all of one game before ultimately succumbing to biceps cramping while warming up in the bullpen over the weekend.
Naturally, New York ruled him out for the contest.
Schmidt said it was precautionary and that he didn't want to push through, but are we really to think that a pitcher who had been sidelined since last summer after undergoing Tommy John surgery and had made a grand total of 30 appearances between 2024 and 2025 is going to magically rebound and be just fine?
Maybe the right-hander really is okay and will be available sooner than we think, but you can't help but feel that Schmidt's playoff status, much like that of Weathers, is now in limbo.
It make Brian Cashman's mind-boggling decision not to acquire relief help last month that much more egregious, and it moves the Yankees even further away from a deep October run, something that was probably already foreign anyway following Aaron Judge's latest trip to the injured list.
Yes, New York picked up John Schreiber on the waiver wire, and he has certainly helped, logging a 2.00 ERA over eight relief appearances. He will almost certainly be on the postseason roster.
But Schreiber alone isn't enough. Not with Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn burning the candle from both ends and Tim Hill turning into a batting practice machine.
Had Weathers and Schmidt remained healthy, there's no question they would have been able to help. It's the fact that Cashman was whimsically relying on it that's so nonsensical.
I've been a big Cashman defender over the years. I think he's been a very good general manager for a long time. But it's becoming harder and harder to defend his decisions.
Just about every other contending team acquired bullpen help at the trade deadline. Apparently, the Yankees were the only ballclub too good to do so.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Varias latas de cerveza fueron vaciadas sobre la cabeza de Aaron Judge mientras el capitán de los Yankees permanecía en el centro del clubhouse de visitantes en el Target Field la semana pasada, rodeado de compañeros eufóricos que celebraban la clasificación del club a la postemporada.
Judge entrecerró los ojos por el ardor y les advirtió a sus compañeros: “Me las van a pagar”.
Aun así, no pretenden que ésa sea su última celebración, pues tienen un firme control del primer puesto del Comodín de la Liga Americana y el título del Este de la Liga Americana todavía está en juego.
“Siempre es bueno cuando puedes celebrar esos momentos durante una temporada”, dijo el manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone. “Mucha gente dedica mucho tiempo, esfuerzo y sudor. Obviamente, éste es apenas el primer paso de lo que esperamos sean muchos”.
Ahora que aseguraron su pase a la postemporada, ¿qué más les espera a los Yankees?
¿Cómo podría quedar el roster para la postemporada?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez 
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Trent Grisham, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos
BD: Ben Rice
LA: Gerrit Cole, Cam Schlittler, Max Fried
R: David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick, Tim Hill, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber, Will Warren, Carlos Rodón
Los Yankees utilizaron a 12 lanzadores y a 14 bateadores cuando recibieron a los Medias Rojas en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, así que partiremos de esa misma premisa para el 2026.
Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles contra Tampa Bay, mientras que Schlittler lo hará el jueves. Mirando hacia adelante, eso sugiere que Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Es posible que los Yankees estén alineando a Cole para abrir el Juego 1 y a Schlittler para el Juego 2. Hasta ahora, han preferido no decir mucho al respecto, salvo por la confirmación de Boone de que Cole realizará una apertura en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Rodón podría estar en el bullpen para la serie. En nuestra proyección del roster lo tenemos activo, mientras que el dominicano Luis Gil y Ryan Yarbrough figuran entre quienes quedarían fuera. Ryan Weathers trabaja para regresar como relevista, pero el tiempo juega en su contra. Si está saludable, podría ocupar el lugar de Fulmer o Schreiber.
Chisholm espera regresar esta semana para la serie contra los Rays tras sufrir un esguince en el pulgar derecho, mientras que Grisham ha mostrado mejoría y podría quedarse con un puesto en los jardines. De no ser así, Max Schuemann está entre las alternativas. Otro aspecto para seguir: ¿Podrían los Yankees incluir a Anthony Volpe en lugar de Rosario? Es una posibilidad que vale la pena considerar.
¿Cuándo comenzará la postemporada?
Si los Yankees terminan disputando la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, ésta empezará el 29 de septiembre. La Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana arrancará el 3 de octubre.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees si la temporada terminara hoy?
En estos momentos, sería una revancha de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, con los Yankees recibiendo a los Medias Rojas en el Bronx. Los Yankees ganaron aquella serie dos victorias por una.
Este año, los Yankees tuvieron marca de 7-6 contra Boston.
¿Todavía pueden ganar el Este de la Liga Americana?
Sí, pero tienen un camino cuesta arriba. Los Yankees tienen por delante cuatro enfrentamientos directos con los Rays a partir del martes en el Yankee Stadium, incluyendo una doble-cartelera para abrir la serie. Tampa Bay domina actualmente la serie particular por 6-3, lo que significa que los Yankees necesitarían barrer para quedarse con el criterio de desempate entre ambos.
¿Quién abriría el Juego 1 por los Yankees?
Como se mencionó anteriormente, Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles frente a Tampa Bay y Schlittler lo hará al día siguiente. Por lo tanto, Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Después de permitir siete jonrones en sus dos aperturas anteriores, Cole mermó las dudas externas sobre una posible apertura en los playoffs con una sólida actuación en Arizona. Fried y Rodón han lidiado con lesiones, pero están recuperando su mejor nivel en el momento indicado.
Warren realizará una apertura más durante la serie contra los Orioles, según Boone, pero llegará a los playoffs como una interesante alternativa para el relevo.
¿Será Judge un factor en los playoffs?
Los Yankees han sido poco específicos sobre el estado de Judge. Boone ha evitado ofrecer un plazo estimado para su recuperación e incluso revelar el grado del tirón en la pantorrilla derecha. En términos generales, hasta un tirón de Grado 1, el de menor gravedad, requiere de dos a tres semanas para una recuperación completa.
Es casi seguro que Judge intentará regresar antes. La primera fecha en la que podría ser activado sería para el Juego 162, el 27 de septiembre. Tal como está el panorama ahora mismo, existe una posibilidad muy real de que los Yankees no cuenten con Judge al menos para una potencial Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Judge dijo que le “gustaría” estar activo para la postemporada y que ése es “el plan”, pero no dijo necesariamente que sería para el 29 de septiembre.
¿Cuáles son las otras preocupaciones en cuanto a lesiones?
Grisham ha avanzado en su programa progresivo de correr y debe de estar disponible para el roster de los playoffs, aunque Boone dijo que no será activado antes de que termine la temporada regular. Chisholm ha estado bateando y realizando tiros, y debe de ser activado durante la serie contra los Rays. Si sufre algún contratiempo, Volpe entraría en consideración.
Y aunque los Yankees no han descartado a Giancarlo Stanton, quien ha estado bateando, han ofrecido pocas novedades sobre su recuperación del más reciente tirón en la pantorrilla.

More than almost any other New York Yankees playoff run, this October's edition will provide either immediate vindication for Brian Cashman's trade deadline strategy or all-new reasons to directly blame him for the team's failure. It should be fascinating to watch, if you don't actually have much emotional energy invested in the team's well-being. Clarke Schmidt's postgame note on Sunday evening was just another reason to be anxious about the way this bullpen was constructed and the amount of variables therein.
Trade deadline predictions for the Yankees' haul this year were astoundingly easy to make. A catcher, first and foremost. An impact bat, that was obvious. And then two bullpen arms to help save their late-inning core from running aground before the year ended. Maybe one would be a certified ace, a tier below Mason Miller, but still devilish. Maybe another would be a bounce back candidate or a never-was, someone who Matt Blake could unearth. Either way, the choices were many, but the outcome was obvious: CashGod would be trading for some relievers. Plural.
But then the deadline came and went. We weren't disappointed by the quality of the haul, but rather in a whole new way. No catcher? No relievers? Was this a mistake? Is the deadline tomorrow?
Nope. Cashman went all in and decided that either the prices were too high or not commensurate with the talent available. Instead, he would look the other way and ignore the rising cost of wear-and-tear in August and piece together some bullpen reinforcements using alternate levers. The waiver wire became his friend. His rotation became a plucking ground, as did his own Injured List. Will Clarke Schmidt, Ryan Weathers, Luis Gil, Will Warren, John Schreiber and Michael Fulmer be more valuable together than any names he could've added on Aug. 3? That's the bet. We'll see. I have my doubts, but he has his agenda.
And, in case you weren't already lacking confidence, Schmidt's bicep barked on Sunday and prevented him from entering the game, a game that ace reliever Brent Headrick lit on fire with an average fastball that dipped about a mile and a half below his standard velocity on the season. Hmm. If only he could've been rested during the dog days of summer.
Clarke Schmidt's worrisome postgame comments, Brent Headrick outing vs. Diamondbacks tell the same Yankees story
So, for the record, that's Schmidt - after one MLB outing this year - admitting that, out of precaution, he stopped warming up when his arm barked. His rehab was also halted along the way when he felt forearm cramping on Aug. 4, just one day post-trade deadline. The Yankees getting him back to the MLB level after a summer 2025 Tommy John surgery is remarkable. This is not someone a team should be relying on to cover meaningful postseason innings. And yet.
Headrick's stumble comes in an otherwise phenomenal year, and even as he's lost some gas down the stretch, he's still managed to mostly make things work. He's an expert at limiting inherited runners from scoring, and he's alternated spotless outings with troublesome ones post-deadline. No one knows for certain whether bringing on an experienced seventh-inning guy or two in early August would've prevented the effects of overuse from piling up on Headrick's left arm, but we do know having a viable alternative now could help them deemphasize Headrick if he's struggling to recapture his former glory. Batters hit .345 off him in 15 August games.
That group of alternatives probably doesn't, or shouldn't, include Schmidt, who's hanging on by a thread. Again, it'll be Cashman's crew - Schreiber, Fulmer, Warren, and maybe Weathers, who won't be rehabbing in a regular season game - vs. the field to see who's better equipped for October. Fascinating, if it weren't so presumptuous.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Los Yankees se fueron del Chase Field con el tipo de derrota que hace que un solo lanzamiento parezca más importante que todo un fin de semana.
Una ventaja de 4-1 se esfumó en la quinta entrada del domingo. La culpa recayó sobre Brent Headrick, el caballo de batalla de los Yankees y cuyo brazo había estado impecable hasta entonces.
Nolan Arenado conectó el golpe que selló la remontada. Su grand slam puso a Arizona por delante y contribuyó a que Nueva York cayera por 8-4 en su último partido fuera de casa de la temporada regular.
La entrada empezó con Will Warren aún defendiendo una ventaja de tres carreras. Arizona llenó las bases con un out antes de que Aaron Boone recurriera al bullpen. Los Yankees ya habían anotado jonrones en la tercera entrada gracias a Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones, una racha que sacó del partido a Corbin Burnes y puso el partido brevemente bajo el control de Nueva York.
Headrick entró con las bases llenas. Eliminó a Geraldo Perdomo por strikeout para conseguir el segundo out y, a continuación, concedió una base por bolas a Corbin Carroll, lo que permitió que entrara una carrera. Arenado mandó la siguiente bola fuera por la línea del campo izquierdo. Un lanzamiento después, la bola se quedó dentro del campo.
Ese jonrón de cuatro carreras cambió el marcador de 4-2 a una ventaja de 6-4 para Arizona. Headrick se llevó la derrota y no se le atribuyó ningún salvamento.
La cifra detrás del Grand Slam es motivo de gran preocupación para los Yankees
El problema más grave salió a la luz tras el partido. La bola rápida de Headrick tenía una velocidad notablemente menor que la que había tenido durante la mayor parte de esta temporada en la que ha destacado. El zurdo alcanzó una media de 92,9 mph con ese lanzamiento el domingo, según una publicación del periodista especializado en los Yankees, Brendan Kuty. Baseball Savant sitúa el promedio de la bola de cuatro costuras de Headrick en 94,2 mph para 2026.
Esa diferencia de 1,3 mph no significa que haya una lesión, y no se ha informado de que Headrick esté lesionado. Pero llega al final de una carga de trabajo como ninguna otra que haya tenido que afrontar como relevista de las Grandes Ligas. Headrick ha jugado 79 partidos y ha lanzado 77 entradas. La MLB lo registra con un balance de 7-4, una efectividad de 2,10, 96 strikeouts, 25 bases por bolas y un WHIP de 1,18.
La publicación de Kuty puso en perspectiva el cambio de velocidad tras la salida más desastrosa de Headrick esta temporada.
«La velocidad media de la bola rápida de Headrick esta noche en Arizona contra los Diamondbacks fue de 92,9 mph», escribió Kuty.
Headrick ha lanzado dos días seguidos en Arizona, lanzando dos tercios de entrada el sábado y otra vez el domingo. Ha sumado 10 ponches en 8 1/3 entradas en septiembre, hasta el domingo.
Headrick se acerca a un hito que pocos Yankees han alcanzado
Lo que diferencia esta temporada de una carga de trabajo habitual como relevista es la frecuencia. Headrick ha lanzado en 79 de los 155 partidos de los Yankees, algo más de la mitad del calendario. La MLB informó el domingo de que solo un lanzador de las Grandes Ligas ha salido al campo más veces esta temporada.
La historia del equipo le da aún más peso a esa cifra. Paul Quantrill estableció el récord de la franquicia de los Yankees con 86 apariciones en 2004. Scott Proctor jugó 83 partidos en 2006. Las 79 de Headrick ya igualan el total de Mike Stanton en 2002 y el de Tom Gordon en 2005. A falta de siete partidos, ya está protagonizando una de las temporadas más intensas en el bullpen que ha vivido la franquicia.
El cambio respecto a 2025 es considerable. Según los datos de la MLB, Headrick lanzó 23 entradas con los Yankees y 24 en la Triple A la temporada pasada. Sus 77 entradas en las Grandes Ligas este año ya superan ese total combinado en 30 entradas.
Este bajón de final de temporada es importante, ya que los Yankees necesitan la mejor versión de octubre .
Las estadísticas de Headrick en toda la temporada siguen convirtiéndolo en una de las piezas más sólidas del bullpen de los Yankees. Solo ha cedido cinco jonrones en los 318 bateadores a los que se ha enfrentado. Ha mantenido a los bateadores diestros en un promedio de .205, según los datos actuales de la MLB sobre estadísticas por tipo de bateador, lo que le ha ayudado a evitar quedarse relegado a un papel de relevo específico para determinados enfrentamientos.
Sus últimas actuaciones no han sido tan buenas. En sus últimas siete salidas, Headrick tiene una efectividad de 4,76 en 5 2/3 entradas. Es una muestra pequeña, pero el momento es clave porque Boone va a necesitar opciones fiables en el bullpen para respaldar a la rotación de la postemporada.
Los Yankees prepararon a Headrick para que tuviera una carga de trabajo más intensa durante el invierno. El entrenador de lanzadores, Matt Blake, ya había identificado la recuperación como el principal reto hace meses, cuando Headrick ya se encontraba entre los relevistas más utilizados de la MLB. La pregunta ahora es si los Yankees podrán reducir su tiempo de juego durante la última semana sin que pierda esa precisión que lo ha convertido en indispensable.
Los Yankees tienen ahora que tomar una decisión sobre el descanso en plena lucha por el título de la División Este de la Liga Americana
Para los Yankees, esta derrota ha puesto las cuentas de la División Este de la Liga Americana al límite. Nueva York tiene un balance de 89-66 y está a seis partidos de Tampa Bay, cuando quedan siete partidos por disputar. Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero ahora empiezan una serie de cuatro partidos en casa contra los Rays con muy poco margen en la lucha por el título de la división.
El domingo también se cerró un balance de 47-34 como visitantes, uno de los mejores registros fuera de casa del béisbol.
Nueva York termina con tres partidos contra Baltimore después de enfrentarse a Tampa Bay. Como ya no hay que viajar después de Arizona y el mes de octubre ya está asegurado, la última semana sirve también para decidir qué lanzadores están listos para la postemporada. Por eso, el estado del cuerpo de lanzadores es casi tan importante como la propia clasificación.
La serie contra los Rays complica esa decisión. Mientras la división siga matemáticamente abierta, los Yankees tienen motivos para usar a sus mejores relevos disponibles en partidos reñidos. Si Tampa Bay se asegura el título, la situación cambia rápidamente. Proteger el brazo de Headrick y que recupere su bola rápida habitual podría llegar a ser más importante que otra entrada decisiva para la clasificación.
El grand slam del domingo seguirá siendo el error más evidente porque decidió el partido. Lo que pasa más desapercibido es lo que los Yankees tienen que vigilar ahora. Headrick ha llevado el peso del bullpen durante seis meses, y su bola rápida llegó a Arizona en su momento más flojo, justo cuando octubre está a la vuelta de la esquina.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees won't win the American League East after dropping two out of three games to the Arizona Diamondbacks and are now looking at another Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox. The rest of this season will now be about figuring out their roster heading into October, and this Rays series won't mean much.
There are plenty of questions from fans about what the roster should look like in the final week of the season. And if you're curious about that, reach out to Joseph Randazzo on X or Instagram at @YankeeLibrarian. Fans can ask anything, from questions about bullpen trust trees to what to do with Jazz Chisholm Jr. when he's activated.
The state of the bullpen
Who do you trust in the bullpen outside of Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick, and David Bednar?@Mattmann1199 on Instagram
At this point, the two best names behind them are Will Warren and John Schreiber. It's likely that they'll be without Ryan Weathers, and that is the name I would have gone with. Now it's probably Schreiber, but I'm not too convinced about this answer.
Since Luis Gil has been blowing 100 out of the bullpen, they can see what they have in him as a pen arm heading into October. None of these answers inspire much, but they have somehow been one of the best bullpens in baseball.
A returning bat
Where should Jazz Chisholm Jr. play when they activate him@theezratakeshita on Instagram
Chisholm should probably go to second base. Volpe has been okay, but since his big debut against the Colorado Rockies, he has gone 7-for-33. He has two doubles, three stolen bases, and two RBI.
Since Boston has a ton of lefty starters, they can probably start a game with Volpe and then go to Chisholm later. That feels like what the Yankees will do, and it's probably the case if Volpe is scorching the ball. Of course, there is still time for Volpe to make things interesting here.
Judge's World Series dreams
The World Series window for Judge is closing. Might he go without ever winning one?@_not_mikeee on Instagram
That is absolutely on the table. There are some great players who have never won a championship. Dan Marino, Barry Bonds, and Henrik Lundqvist never got their ring. Granted, the Scott Hunter character in Heated Rivalry feels like it's loosely based on mid-2010s Lundqvist, but that might only half-count since it's a work of fiction.
A wild storyline would be the Yankees winning a World Series this year without Judge. Imagine the chaos of his legacy talks if that happens.
Job statuses
Is there a scenario that gets Cash or Boone fired this year?@kirby.phillips7 on Instagram
These questions are always easy to answer. Probably not this year. Cashman will probably go out on his own accord. Boone is the most likely candidate to get fired, but there aren't many teams that are going to axe a manager who kept their team afloat and in postseason contention with the amount of injuries they had. When baseball comes back after the lockout, those two will probably still be here.
Missing the playoffs again might do it for them, but the last time that happened, they stayed. It does feel like they have unlimited security in New York.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.
